m3pgi3: This week you review two classes that are often used together when you tell or explain something: **impersonal se** (_se corta, se cortan, no se puede_), for instructions and rules that apply to everyone, and **connectors** (_primero, luego, como, por eso, así que, al final_), to put events in order and explain why they happen. The setting: a Nicaraguan cooking course in Managua.
qv9tls: Se + verb: what matters is what gets done
1o46e24: In recipes, signs, manuals and rules it doesn't matter **who** does the action: it's information for anyone. That's why we use **se + verb in the third person**: _se pela el plátano_, _aquí se habla inglés_, _¿cómo se escribe tu apellido?_
19voqxe: The verb **agrees with the thing**: one thing or something uncountable → singular (_se lava **el arroz**_); several things → plural (_se lavan **los frijoles**_). The thing can go before or after: _las ollas se guardan aquí_ = _aquí se guardan las ollas_.
1sljzy6: If there's no thing, the verb is **singular**: _en esta casa se come temprano_, _en el mercado se regatea_.
hfpz1j: One thing, several things or none
1ih3vu5: Rules: se puede, no se puede, and who's who
mphzh: For permission and bans you use **se puede / no se puede + infinitive**. The verb _poder_ is always **singular**, because what follows is an infinitive: _no se puede entrar con sandalias_, _se puede pagar con tarjeta_.
1kif5kl: Compare three different sentences: _Se corta el pan_ (an instruction for everyone), _Marcos, corta el pan_ (an imperative to one specific person) and _Marcos corta el pan_ (you say what Marcos does).
76o6y8: Don't confuse it with **reflexive se**: _Marcos se lava las manos_ (himself). In impersonal se there is no person: _primero se lavan las manos_ (everyone, anyone).
1kgd819: Before you write, find the thing: one or several? If an infinitive follows the verb, the verb is singular.
1g1c76q: With an infinitive, _poder_ is singular: **no se puede**.
ifczwm: Without _se_, the sentence talks about one specific person (he or she).
18vs2cu: Telling things in order: primero, luego, al final
9oph8u: To make a story or instructions easy to follow, mark the order: **primero** → **luego / después** → **entonces** → **al final** or **por último**.
1fzdgpy: **Al final** says how the story ended (_al final comimos todos juntos_). **Por último** introduces the last step of a list (_por último, se sirve caliente_).
du5sv5: **Después** goes alone or with **de + infinitive**: _después, lavamos todo_; _después de lavar todo, nos fuimos_. Never _después de, llegó_. And **entonces** has two uses: _at that moment_ (_entonces sonó el teléfono_) or _so_ (_no había gas, entonces cocinamos con leña_).
6j2t7s: _Después de_ needs an infinitive or a noun: _después de comer_.
1qxmink: Explaining why: porque, como, por eso, así que, es decir
1sowqau: For the **cause**: **porque** goes after what happened (_llegué tarde porque no había buses_); **como** goes at the start, before what happened (_como no había buses, llegué tarde_).
1kbuip8: For the **consequence**: **por eso** and **así que** go after the cause (_no había buses, **por eso** llegué tarde_; _tenía hambre, **así que** compré un vigorón_). Direction matters: first the cause, then the result.
yp5uaf: To **clarify** or say the same thing in other words: **es decir** (and in conversation, **o sea**): _el frijol se remoja, es decir, se deja en agua toda la noche_.
i6cbl8: Ask yourself: what came first, the cause or the result? Cause at the start → _como_. Result at the start → _porque_. Cause and then result → _por eso_ or _así que_.
1w78q: Causal **como** goes at the start. To put the cause after, use **porque**.
ewc021: **Por eso** goes after the cause: first _no había mesas_.

1wgrifa: Connectors are signals for the listener: _primero, luego, entonces, como, así que_. If you say them fast and without a pause, the story sounds like one long sentence.
1qn3mjj: After a sequence connector (_primero, luego, al final, por último_) make a **short pause** and keep the pitch **slightly up**: _Primero ↗ | se lava el arroz_. In writing, the pause is the comma.
1v4u9f: With causal **como**, the voice rises at the end of the cause and falls at the end of the result: _Como no había gas ↗ | cocinamos con leña ↘_. With **así que** and **por eso**, the pause comes before: _no había gas | así que cocinamos con leña_.
ec6nor: In writing, the pause is a **comma**: after _primero, luego, al final, por último_ and after the cause with _como_ (_Como llovía, …_). A comma is also usually put before _así que_ and _por eso_.
